Name: American Computer Science League (ACSL)
Description: A multi-division computer science competition for K-12 schools covering fundamental concepts from number systems to graph theory and programming.

Name: MIT THINK Scholars Program
Description: An educational initiative by MIT students offering high schoolers mentorship and funding to complete self-directed STEM research projects.

Name: BioEHSC High School Bioengineering Competition
Description: A team-based design competition hosted by UC Berkeley where high school students develop bioengineering solutions to current medical problems.

Name: American Association of Physics Teachers Photo Contest
Description: An international competition where students submit a photo illustrating a physics concept alongside a written essay explaining the science.

Name: Stockholm Junior Water Prize
Description: A national water-related research competition for high school students focusing on water quality, resource management, and environmental science.

Name: Genius Olympiad
Description: An international high school project competition focusing on environmental issues through science, writing, engineering, and design.

Name: Harvard MIT Mathematics Tournament (HMMT)
Description: One of the largest student-run math competitions in the world, held semi-annually for high-school students on Harvard and MIT campuses.

Name: Princeton University Physics Competition (PUPC)
Description: An international physics contest organized by Princeton undergraduates testing advanced problem-solving and mechanics skills.

Name: International Physics Olympiad Screening (USAPhO)
Description: The second round qualification exam following the F=ma contest to select the United States Physics Team representatives.

Name: American Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad (USAAAO)
Description: A national organization running selection exams for high school students interested in astrophysics, cosmology, and observational astronomy.

Name: National Cyber Scholarship Foundation Contest
Description: A nation-wide cybersecurity gamified challenge awarding scholarships and training to high school students through CyberStart America.

Name: PicoCTF Cybersecurity Competition
Description: A free online capture-the-flag cybersecurity framework created by Carnegie Mellon University experts for high school students.

Name: Girls Who Code Summer Immersion Program
Description: A free 2-week virtual program for female and non-binary students to learn computer science concepts, web development, and UX design.

Name: Kode With Klossy Camp
Description: A two-week coding camp for young women and non-binary youth exploring web development, mobile apps, data science, and AI.

Name: Stanford Mathematics Camp (SUMaC)
Description: An intensive summer program for mathematically talented high school sophomores and juniors focused on advanced math topics.

Name: MathILy - Serious Mathematics Infused with Levity
Description: A 5-week residential summer program for mathematically talented high school students centered on undergraduate-level discrete mathematics.

Name: Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists (PROMYS)
Description: A six-week summer program at Boston University designed to encourage high school students to explore the creative world of mathematics.

Name: Arnold O. Beckman High School Internship Program
Description: A research internship offering high school students direct hands-on laboratory research experience alongside university faculty.

Name: Navy Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP)
Description: An eight-week paid summer internship program placing high school students in Department of Navy laboratories across the US.

Name: NASA High School Internship Program
Description: Paid internship opportunities for high school students to participate in research and operational missions across various NASA centers.

Name: Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Scholar Program
Description: Paid summer internship opportunities for high school students working alongside university personnel and AFRL scientists on defense STEM projects.

Name: National Institute of Standards and Technology (SHIP)
Description: The Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP) offers research opportunities to juniors and seniors interested in physical sciences and engineering.

Name: High School Mathematical Contest in Modeling (HiMCM)
Description: An international contest designed to offer high school students the opportunity to work as team members to solve real-world modeling problems.

Name: Fermat Math Contest (Waterloo)
Description: A 25-question multiple-choice contest organized by the Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC) at the University of Waterloo.

Name: Euclid Mathematics Contest
Description: A premier senior-level mathematical competition written by high school students to demonstrate creative problem-solving and written proofs.

Name: Caribou Mathematics Competition
Description: A worldwide online math contest held six times per school year that focuses on logic, puzzle solving, and creative math problems.

Name: FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC)
Description: A robotics competition where student teams design, build, program, and operate robots to compete in an alliance format.

Name: VEX Robotics Competition
Description: A global robotics competition that fosters STEM skills through hands-on, team-based robot construction and programming challenges.

Name: Technovation Girls
Description: A global tech entrepreneurship competition where young women build a mobile app or AI prototype to address a problem in their community.

Name: CyberPatriot National Youth Cyber Defense Competition
Description: The nation's largest youth cybersecurity contest putting high school teams in the position of newly hired IT professionals managing network systems.

Name: National Science Bowl
Description: A fast-paced jeopardy-style academic competition organized by the U.S. Department of Energy testing all areas of science and mathematics.

Name: Envirothon Competition
Description: An environmental and natural resource competition for high school students testing knowledge in aquatic ecology, forestry, soils, and wildlife.
